html:
A Greek scholar born in Cyrene about 276 BCE who became chief librarian of the Library of Alexandria. He is best known for measuring the size of the Earth.

He knew that at noon on midsummer day the Sun stood straight overhead at Syene (modern Aswan), while at Alexandria, to the north, it cast a shadow at an angle of about one fiftieth of a circle. Taking the distance between the two cities, he worked out the Earth's circumference. Depending on the length of his stadion, his answer was close to the true figure.

He was also a geographer, and is credited with coining the word. He drew a map of the known world with lines of latitude and longitude, and dated events from the fall of Troy onward. In mathematics the sieve of Eratosthenes for finding prime numbers is his. He was a friend of Archimedes. Because he was good at many things but first at none, rivals called him "Beta". He worked under the patronage of Ptolemaic Egypt.
sum: A Greek scholar born in Cyrene about 276 BCE who became chief librarian of the Library of Alexandria. He is best known for measuring the size of the Earth.
